Phase 2 sequencing - proposal
Hello both,

Following our conversation, a proposal for how we sequence Phase 2.

Rather than delivering all four fresh categories together in one go-live, we would
deliver produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery. Three smaller
go-lives roughly six weeks apart.

The advantage is that value starts landing earlier and each wave de-risks the next. The
disadvantage is more cutover events and a longer total elapsed time, which I know is in
tension with the twelve-month window.

If this works for you we would build the plan around it. Happy to discuss.

Q1 2026 waste reporting - fresh
Hello,

First full quarter of fresh live. Numbers against the baseline we agreed in December.

Produce and dairy, 25 pilot stores, January to March:

  Fresh waste            4.1% -> 3.4% of fresh net sales
  Absolute reduction     approximately 118 tonnes over the quarter
  Estimated CO2e avoided approximately 296 tonnes
  Availability           +1.9 points
  Order automation       88% on the categories in scope

The CO2e figure uses the conversion factors in your own sustainability report rather
than ours, so it should reconcile with what you publish.

Chilled ready meals is not in these numbers, it went live too late in the quarter.

Two caveats. The baseline quarter had an unusually warm February which flatters produce.
And the 118 tonnes is scaled from 25 stores, so please do not multiply it up to the full
estate in any external communication without talking to us first.

One note on how it is arrived at. The tonnage is derived from the article movement totals
in the nightly extract, not counted from till data. That is the normal basis and it has
been stable all quarter, but it is a derivation rather than a count and I would rather say
so than have it come up later.
